 JUSTICE G. SATAPATHY  ORDER(ORAL)

03. 1.
This matter is taken up through Hybrid Arrangement (Virtual/Physical Mode).

2. This is an application U/S.483 of BNSS by the petitioner for grant of bail in connection with CT Case No. 630 of 2025 arising out of Gurudijhatia PS Case No. 171 of 2025 pending in the file of learned SDJM, Athagarh for commission of offences punishable Under Sections 274/318(4)/318(2)/316(3)/3(5) of BNS and Sections 51 and 59 of Food Safety and Standards Act,
2006 (in short "the Act"), on the main allegation of adulterating milk rendering it unfit for human consumption.

3. Heard, Mr. Jugala Kishore Panda, learned counsel for the petitioner and Mr. A. Pradhan, learned Additional Public Prosecutor in the matter and perused the record together with copy of charge sheet, Certified Copy of the FIR, Forwarding Report, Statement of witnesses, Spot Map, Seizure Memo and Orders disclosing grant of bail to co-accused persons in ABLAPL Nos. 11098 & 11147 of 2025.

On being queried about the criminal antecedent of the petitioner, Mr. Panda volunteers to withhold bail to the petitioner, if he is found to have any criminal antecedents of similar nature for commission of offence under Food Safety and Standard Act, 2006 4.

After having considered the rival submissions upon perusal of record, there appears allegation against the Petitioner for adulterating milk rendering it unfit for human consumption, but the sample analysis report submitted by Food Analyst reveals the quality of the milk sample taken from Prakash Khuntia @ Prakash vs State Of Odisha ... Opposite Party on 25 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/136211501/
1 allegedly seized adulterated milk is unsafe U/S. 3.1.(zz) of the Act for containing foreign fat like butyro, however, the Petitioner is in custody since 12.09.2025 and in the meantime, charge sheet has already been submitted and none of the penal offences imposed against the Petitioner prescribes punishment beyond seven years, but the punishment prescribes for offence U/S. 59(iv) of the Act is for maximum punishment up to life in case, the contravention of such offence results in death and in this case, no such death of any person has occurred.

sentences.text: In such view of the matter and taking into consideration the nature and gravity of the offences as alleged against the petitioner vis--vis the accusations sought to be brought against him and keeping in view the inherent right of an accused to be presumed innocent until proven guilty at the trial, this Court without expressing any view on merits admits the Petitioner to bail, but subject to verification of his criminal antecedent for similar nature.

5. Hence, the bail application of the petitioner stands allowed and he is allowed to go on bail on furnishing bail bonds of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand) with two solvent sureties each for the like amount to the satisfaction of the learned Court in seisin of the case on such terms and conditions as deem fit and proper by it.

In view of the specific submission as advanced for the petitioner, the aforesaid order shall not be extended to the petitioner, if he is found to have any criminal antecedent of similar nature for commission of offences under Food Safety and Standard Act, 2006.
6.
Accordingly, the BLAPL stands disposed of.

7. Issue urgent certified copy of the order as per Rules.
